requirements.quote: The variable length "extension bytes" are part of the fixed header, not the variable header.
requirements.condition: When encoding or parsing the variable-length extension bytes
requirements.required_behavior: Treat the extension bytes as part of the fixed header.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Treat the extension bytes as part of the variable header.
requirements.why_checkable: Header parsing or serialization can verify the section to which these bytes are assigned.

requirements.quote: It resides between the fixed header and the payload.
requirements.condition: When an MQTT command message contains a variable header
requirements.required_behavior: Place the variable header after the fixed header and before the payload.
requirements.why_checkable: The encoded field order can be inspected directly.

requirements.quote: The format of the variable header fields are described in the following topics, in the order in which they must appear in the header:
requirements.condition: When encoding variable-header fields
requirements.required_behavior: Emit the fields in the specified order.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Emit variable-header fields in a different order.
requirements.why_checkable: A serialized variable header can be checked for field ordering.

requirements.quote: The variable length Remaining Length field is not part of the variable header.
requirements.condition: When encoding or parsing the Remaining Length field
requirements.required_behavior: Treat Remaining Length as outside the variable header.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Treat Remaining Length as part of the variable header.
requirements.why_checkable: The parser or serializer's header boundaries can be inspected.

requirements.quote: The bytes of the Remaining Length field do not contribute to the byte count of the Remaining Length value. This value only takes account of the variable header and the payload.
requirements.condition: When calculating the Remaining Length value
requirements.required_behavior: Count only the variable header and payload bytes.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Include the bytes encoding the Remaining Length field itself.
requirements.why_checkable: The declared value can be compared with the exact encoded lengths of the variable header and payload.

requirements.quote: The protocol name is present in the variable header of a MQTT CONNECT message.
requirements.condition: For an MQTT CONNECT message
requirements.required_behavior: Include the protocol name in the variable header.
requirements.why_checkable: CONNECT variable-header fields can be inspected for presence.

requirements.quote: This field is a UTF-encoded string that represents the protocol name MQIsdp, capitalized as shown.
requirements.condition: When encoding the CONNECT protocol-name field
requirements.required_behavior: Encode the field as a UTF-encoded string with the value MQIsdp and the shown capitalization.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Use a differently capitalized or otherwise different protocol-name value.
requirements.why_checkable: The field's encoding and decoded string value can be compared exactly.

requirements.quote: The protocol version is present in the variable header of a CONNECT message.
requirements.condition: For a CONNECT message
requirements.required_behavior: Include the protocol-version field in the variable header.
requirements.why_checkable: CONNECT variable-header fields can be inspected for presence.

requirements.quote: The field is an 8-bit unsigned value that represents the revision level of the protocol used by the client.
requirements.condition: When encoding or parsing the protocol-version field
requirements.required_behavior: Represent it as an 8-bit unsigned value.
requirements.why_checkable: The field width and numeric representation are directly observable.

requirements.quote: The value of the Protocol version field for the current version of the protocol, 3 (0x03), is shown in the table below.
requirements.condition: When a client uses the current protocol version described by this chunk
requirements.required_behavior: Set the Protocol version field to 3 (0x03).
requirements.why_checkable: The single encoded version byte can be compared with 0x03.

requirements.quote: The Clean start, Will, Will QoS, and Retain flags are present in the variable header of a CONNECT message.
requirements.condition: For a CONNECT message
requirements.required_behavior: Include the Clean start, Will, Will QoS, and Retain flags in its variable header.
requirements.why_checkable: The CONNECT variable header and its Connect flags byte can be inspected.

requirements.quote: Position: bit 1 of the Connect flags byte.
requirements.condition: When encoding or parsing the Clean start flag
requirements.required_behavior: Use bit 1 of the Connect flags byte.
requirements.why_checkable: The flag's bit position is directly testable.

requirements.quote: If the flag is set, the broker discards any outstanding messages, deletes all subscriptions for the client, and resets the Message ID to 1.
requirements.condition: When the Clean start flag is set
requirements.required_behavior: Discard all outstanding messages for the client.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Preserve outstanding messages from the client's previous state.
requirements.why_checkable: Broker state can be populated before connection and inspected afterward.

requirements.quote: If the flag is set, the broker discards any outstanding messages, deletes all subscriptions for the client, and resets the Message ID to 1.
requirements.condition: When the Clean start flag is set
requirements.required_behavior: Delete all subscriptions for the client.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Preserve the client's previous subscriptions.
requirements.why_checkable: Subscription state can be populated before connection and inspected afterward.

requirements.quote: If the flag is set, the broker discards any outstanding messages, deletes all subscriptions for the client, and resets the Message ID to 1.
requirements.condition: When the Clean start flag is set
requirements.required_behavior: Reset the Message ID to 1.
requirements.why_checkable: The broker's next or current Message ID can be observed after processing CONNECT.

requirements.quote: Bits 7, 6, and 0 of this byte are not used in the current version of the protocol. They are reserved for future use.
requirements.condition: For the Connect flags byte in the current protocol version
requirements.required_behavior: Leave bits 7, 6, and 0 unused and reserved.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Assign current-protocol flag semantics to bits 7, 6, or 0.
requirements.why_checkable: Flag definitions and emitted Connect flag values can be checked for use of the reserved positions.

requirements.quote: Position: bit 2 of the Connect flags byte.
requirements.condition: When encoding or parsing the Will flag
requirements.required_behavior: Use bit 2 of the Connect flags byte.
requirements.why_checkable: The flag's bit position is directly testable.

requirements.quote: The Will message defines that a message is published on behalf of the client by the broker when either an I/O error is encountered by the broker during communication with the client, or the client fails to communicate within the Keep Alive timer schedule.
requirements.condition: When the broker encounters an I/O error while communicating with a client having a configured Will message
requirements.required_behavior: Publish the Will message on behalf of the client.
requirements.why_checkable: An I/O failure can be induced and resulting broker publications observed.

requirements.quote: The Will message defines that a message is published on behalf of the client by the broker when either an I/O error is encountered by the broker during communication with the client, or the client fails to communicate within the Keep Alive timer schedule.
requirements.condition: When a client having a configured Will message fails to communicate within the Keep Alive timer schedule
requirements.required_behavior: Publish the Will message on behalf of the client.
requirements.why_checkable: Client silence can be induced and resulting broker publications observed.

requirements.quote: Sending a Will message is not triggered by the broker receiving a DISCONNECT message from the client.
requirements.condition: When the broker receives a DISCONNECT message from the client
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Trigger sending the client's Will message because of that DISCONNECT.
requirements.why_checkable: A client can send DISCONNECT and observers can verify that no Will publication is triggered.

requirements.quote: If the Will flag is set, the Will QoS and Will Retain fields must be present in the Connect flags byte, and the Will Topic and Will Message fields must be present in the payload.
requirements.condition: When the Will flag is set
requirements.required_behavior: Include the Will QoS and Will Retain fields in the Connect flags byte.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Omit either the Will QoS or Will Retain field.
requirements.why_checkable: The Connect flags byte can be inspected for both fields.

requirements.quote: If the Will flag is set, the Will QoS and Will Retain fields must be present in the Connect flags byte, and the Will Topic and Will Message fields must be present in the payload.
requirements.condition: When the Will flag is set
requirements.required_behavior: Include the Will Topic and Will Message fields in the payload.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Omit either the Will Topic or Will Message field.
requirements.why_checkable: The CONNECT payload can be parsed and checked for both fields.

requirements.quote: Position: bits 4 and 3 of the Connect flags byte.
requirements.condition: When encoding or parsing Will QoS
requirements.required_behavior: Use bits 4 and 3 of the Connect flags byte.
requirements.why_checkable: The field's bit positions are directly testable.

requirements.quote: If the Will flag is set, the Will QoS field is mandatory, otherwise its value is disregarded.
requirements.condition: When the Will flag is set
requirements.required_behavior: Provide the Will QoS field.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Omit the Will QoS field.
requirements.why_checkable: A CONNECT packet with Will enabled can be checked for the field.

requirements.quote: If the Will flag is set, the Will QoS field is mandatory, otherwise its value is disregarded.
requirements.condition: When the Will flag is not set
requirements.required_behavior: Disregard the value of the Will QoS field.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Apply Will QoS semantics when Will is disabled.
requirements.why_checkable: Different Will QoS bit values with Will disabled can be tested for lack of behavioral effect.

requirements.quote: The value of Will QoS is 0 (0x00), 1 (0x01), or 2 (0x02).
requirements.condition: When a Will QoS value is used
requirements.required_behavior: Use one of 0, 1, or 2.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Use a Will QoS value outside 0, 1, or 2.
requirements.why_checkable: The two-bit field can be decoded and compared with the allowed enumeration.

requirements.quote: Position: bit 5 of the Connect flags byte.
requirements.condition: When encoding or parsing the Will Retain flag
requirements.required_behavior: Use bit 5 of the Connect flags byte.
requirements.why_checkable: The flag's bit position is directly testable.

requirements.quote: The Will Retain flag indicates whether or not broker should retain the Will message which is published by the broker on behalf of the client in the event that the client is disconnected unexpectedly.
requirements.condition: When a client is disconnected unexpectedly and the broker publishes its Will message
requirements.required_behavior: Use the Will Retain flag to determine whether the broker retains that Will message.
requirements.why_checkable: Unexpected disconnection can be induced and retained-message state observed for both flag values.

requirements.quote: The Will Retain flag is mandatory if the Will flag is set, otherwise, it is disregarded.
requirements.condition: When the Will flag is set
requirements.required_behavior: Provide the Will Retain flag.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Omit the Will Retain flag.
requirements.why_checkable: A CONNECT packet with Will enabled can be checked for the flag.

requirements.quote: The Will Retain flag is mandatory if the Will flag is set, otherwise, it is disregarded.
requirements.condition: When the Will flag is not set
requirements.required_behavior: Disregard the Will Retain flag.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Apply Will Retain semantics when Will is disabled.
requirements.why_checkable: Both Will Retain bit values can be tested with Will disabled for lack of behavioral effect.

requirements.quote: The Keep Alive timer is present in the variable header of a MQTT CONNECT message.
requirements.condition: For an MQTT CONNECT message
requirements.required_behavior: Include the Keep Alive timer in the variable header.
requirements.why_checkable: The CONNECT variable header can be parsed for field presence.

requirements.quote: The Keep Alive timer, measured in seconds, defines the maximum time interval between messages received from a client.
requirements.condition: When interpreting the Keep Alive timer
requirements.required_behavior: Interpret its unit as seconds and its value as the maximum interval between client messages.
requirements.why_checkable: Timing behavior can be compared with the encoded value in seconds.

requirements.quote: The client has a responsibility to send a message within each Keep Alive time period.
requirements.condition: When Keep Alive is active
requirements.required_behavior: Send at least one message within each Keep Alive time period.
requirements.why_checkable: Client network output can be observed over a Keep Alive interval.

requirements.quote: In the absence of a data-related message during the time period, the client sends a PINGREQ message, which the broker acknowledges with a PINGRESP message.
requirements.condition: When the client has sent no data-related message during a Keep Alive period
requirements.required_behavior: Send a PINGREQ message.
requirements.why_checkable: Client output during an otherwise idle interval can be observed.

requirements.quote: In the absence of a data-related message during the time period, the client sends a PINGREQ message, which the broker acknowledges with a PINGRESP message.
requirements.condition: When the broker receives the client's Keep Alive PINGREQ
requirements.required_behavior: Acknowledge it with a PINGRESP message.
requirements.why_checkable: A PINGREQ can be injected and the broker response inspected.

requirements.quote: If the broker does not receive a message from the client within one and a half times the Keep Alive time period (the client is allowed "grace" of half a time period), it disconnects the client as if the client had sent a DISCONNECT message.
requirements.condition: When the broker receives no client message within one and a half times the Keep Alive period
requirements.required_behavior: Disconnect the client and process the disconnection as if the client had sent DISCONNECT.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Keep the client connected beyond that timeout because of continued silence.
requirements.error_behavior: Disconnect the client as if it had sent a DISCONNECT message.
requirements.why_checkable: Client silence can be induced and both disconnect timing and resulting state transition observed.

requirements.quote: This action does not impact any of the client's subscriptions.
requirements.condition: When the broker disconnects a silent client after one and a half Keep Alive periods
requirements.required_behavior: Preserve the client's subscriptions.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Remove or alter the client's subscriptions because of this timeout disconnection.
requirements.why_checkable: Subscriptions can be created before the timeout and inspected afterward.

requirements.quote: The Keep Alive timer is a 16-bit value that represents the number of seconds for the time period.
requirements.condition: When encoding or parsing the Keep Alive timer
requirements.required_behavior: Represent it as a 16-bit value whose unit is seconds.
requirements.why_checkable: The field width and time-unit interpretation can be tested directly.

requirements.quote: A value of zero (0) means the client is not disconnected.
requirements.condition: When the Keep Alive timer value is zero
requirements.required_behavior: Do not disconnect the client due to the Keep Alive timeout.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Apply the Keep Alive timeout disconnection to the client.
requirements.why_checkable: A zero-valued CONNECT can be followed by extended silence while observing connection state.

requirements.quote: The ordering of the 2 bytes of the Keep Alive Timer is MSB, then LSB (big-endian).
requirements.condition: When encoding or parsing the two-byte Keep Alive timer
requirements.required_behavior: Order the bytes most-significant byte first, then least-significant byte.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Encode or interpret the field as little-endian.
requirements.why_checkable: The two serialized bytes can be compared with a known multi-byte value.

requirements.quote: The connect return code is resent in the variable header of a MQTT CONNACK message.
requirements.condition: For an MQTT CONNACK message
requirements.required_behavior: Include the connect return code in the variable header.
requirements.why_checkable: The CONNACK variable header can be parsed for field presence.

requirements.quote: This field defines a one byte unsigned return code.
requirements.condition: When encoding or parsing the connect return code
requirements.required_behavior: Represent it as a one-byte unsigned value.
requirements.why_checkable: The field width and unsigned numeric representation are directly observable.
